ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, $C$ is a point on the line segment $AB$, $M$ is the midpoint of $AC$, and $N$ is the midpoint of $BC$. If $MC$ is $2\,\text{cm}$ longer than $NC$, how much longer is $AC$ than $BC$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Given that $M$ is the midpoint of $AC$, and $N$ is the midpoint of $BC$,
\\
hence $MC=\frac{1}{2}AC$, $CN=\frac{1}{2}BC$,
\\
since $MC-NC=2cm$,
\\
it follows that $\frac{1}{2}AC-\frac{1}{2}BC=2cm$,
\\
therefore $AC-BC=\boxed{4cm}$.
